question: Can every positive target, including both same-scene sibling-door queries, supply a materially displaced second query observation while the exact foreign target remains outside the negative view?

predecessor.single_change: Move the active observation from the bound reference trajectory to the query trajectory. Select the maximum available fully visible baseline in the same fixed 0.05-1.10m interval before opening RGB or calling a model; retain the exact-target-absent sibling negatives.

selection.ranking: Maximum available fully visible baseline up to 1.10m, then minimum frame gap, maximum depth-visible ratio, visible vertices and projected area, then earliest frame; same-scene negative frames additionally require zero projected vertices from the exact foreign target.

forbidden_after_freeze: open candidate RGB or call a model before all active query frames are fixed
change reachability, visibility, exact-target absence or ranking after observing selected RGB
replace an active frame after downstream failure
use provider geometry or target identity in a runtime binding decision
claim provider-selected recorded views prove a user can execute the observation action
claim_boundary: This zero-model source assessment uses privileged 3RScan pose, depth and registered instance geometry to freeze recorded active query views for three consumed targets and preserve two exact-target-absent sibling-door negatives. It measures source reachability only; it is not runtime binding, arbitrary sibling rejection, provider-independent generalization, user-action feasibility, named entrance, ownership, access, traversability, waypoint, arrival, handoff, Android deployment, benefit, reliability or safety evidence.
